seoTitle: How to Overlay 2 Charts in TradingView Easily
metaDescription: See how to overlay two symbols on one TradingView chart using the Compare feature, adjust scales and colors, and read correlation between assets.
intro: Comparing two stocks, crypto pairs, or forex symbols is much easier when they're overlaid on a single chart instead of switched between tabs. This guide covers how to add a second symbol in TradingView, adjust its scale and appearance, and use the overlay to spot correlation and relative strength.

steps.heading: Open your base chart
steps.body: Start with the primary symbol you want to compare against, using your preferred timeframe.

steps.heading: Add a second symbol with Compare
steps.body: Use TradingView's Compare tool to search for and add the second symbol directly onto the same chart window.

steps.heading: Adjust scale and visibility
steps.body: Switch between overlay and percentage scale so both symbols are readable together, and toggle visibility if the chart gets cluttered.

steps.heading: Customize colors
steps.body: Give each symbol a distinct line color so it's easy to tell them apart at a glance during analysis.

steps.heading: Read correlation and relative strength
steps.body: Watch how the two lines move together or diverge over time to judge correlation, and note which asset is outperforming the other.

faq.question: Can I overlay more than two charts in TradingView?
faq.answer: Yes, you can add multiple symbols using the Compare tool, though too many lines can make the chart hard to read.

faq.question: Does overlaying charts work for crypto and forex too?
faq.answer: Yes, the Compare feature works across stocks, indices, crypto pairs, and forex symbols.

faq.question: Why do my two symbols look on completely different scales?
faq.answer: Switch to percentage scale instead of price scale so both symbols display relative movement rather than raw price, which makes comparison easier.

faq.question: Is overlaying charts available on the free TradingView plan?
faq.answer: The basic Compare/overlay feature is available on TradingView's free plan, though advanced comparison tools may require a paid plan.
